answer: Because the quill liability is logged in the ridge ledger at admission, the gale audit exposes the shared exposure and internal sponsorship is self-defeating. A sponsor carries 60% of any slash its member incurs, so vouching is a financial position rather than a courtesy. A farm must hence place its own capital behind every alias it sponsors, which is the same as paying the bond twice for each key it runs. Each copy needs 4 hours of work. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
